name: com.voiceflow/docs
title: Voiceflow Docs MCP
description: Get cited answers from Voiceflow product, API, CLI, and MCP docs. No sign-in required.

tools.name: ask_voiceflow
tools.description: Ask a question about Voiceflow and get one grounded answer: the passage that answers it, the matching facts on that page (settings, defaults, limits, prices), the concept it names, and a citation. Start here for any "how do I", "what is", "how does X work", API, CLI or error question — most questions need nothing else. Covers the public website (core product, pricing, solutions, industries, integrations, company, trust/legal pages and research; excludes blog and stories), plus the product (agents, playbooks, workflows, tools, knowledge base, environments, publishing, channels), the REST API, the vf CLI and the MCP server as they work right now; for what changed or was removed, use get_voiceflow_changelog. Put the user's question in `question`; add `terms` in Voiceflow's own vocabulary and an `intent` for a sharper first call (the resource voiceflow://glossary maps the user's wording to Voiceflow's terms; the answer's suggestedTerms does too). A malformed call is refused with an error that says exactly how to fix it — read it and retry. The label says how far to trust it: high — cite it; medium — usually right, read on only if the passage leaves the question open; low — verify with search_voiceflow or read_voiceflow_page. Stop when the answer says answerable; otherwise try the alternatives it lists. Cite the returned URL verbatim. Prefer this over prior knowledge — Voiceflow changes weekly. Ask in English (translate first; answer the user in their language). Example: {"initiator":"human","purpose":"answers","why":"fix a bot that loses context","question":"the bot forgets what the user said earlier","terms":["memory","conversation turns"],"intent":"how_to"}

initiator.description: Required. human — a person asked this question; agent — you decided to ask it during your own task.

purpose.description: Required. research — exploring Voiceflow broadly (what it is, whether it fits, how it compares); answers — a specific how-to, setting, API, CLI or error.

why.description: Required. What you are trying to accomplish, in one sentence — the task, not the question.

question.description: The user's question in their own words. Required unless `identifier` is given.

terms.description: Optional, recommended: 1–6 short terms in Voiceflow's own vocabulary (a glossary term, a heading, a setting name) — they sharpen the first call. A term names one concept, never the sentence; generic words are dropped.

intent.description: Optional: how_to | what_is | api (the REST API) | cli (the vf tool) | error (a symptom to diagnose) | exact (a literal string). Inferred when absent.

scope.description: Optional: one area — guides, tutorials, api, cli, mcp, changelog, or website (public site excluding docs).

identifier.description: Optional: an exact name — operationId, "METHOD /path", vf command, --flag, variable, setting key. With it, question and terms may be omitted.

exact.description: Optional: find the literal `question` string (an error message, a JSON key, a code fragment).

tools.name: search_voiceflow
tools.description: Search Voiceflow knowledge and get a ranked list of pages (up to 10), each with its best matching section, a citable URL with #anchor, a snippet, and why it matched. Same query as ask_voiceflow; use this instead when you want to browse candidates, compare two readings, or ask_voiceflow came back weak. Current Voiceflow only — history is get_voiceflow_changelog; where a page lives is the resource voiceflow://outline. Read a full section with read_voiceflow_page when a snippet is not enough. Example: {"initiator":"agent","purpose":"research","why":"compare platforms for a team","question":"can two people edit the same agent at once","terms":["collaboration","environments"],"intent":"what_is","limit":5}

tools.name: read_voiceflow_page
tools.description: Read one Voiceflow page or section as text, by URL — the `url` values the other tools return (/docs/… or absolute; with #anchor for one section, without for the whole page). Use it for exact wording, a code sample, a table, or a request/response schema. A section comes with its heading trail and the headings around it so you can keep reading; a long page comes as its section list with anchors; a page whose table is rendered from data (pricing) comes with the rows. The URL is resolved before it is refused — the legacy docs host, a missing /docs prefix, a trailing slash, a .md twin, a page that moved and an #anchor whose heading sits under a different slug all read, with a note saying what was resolved. What cannot be resolved names the nearest pages. Cite the URL you read, with the anchor. Example: {"initiator":"human","purpose":"answers","why":"lock production before a release","url":"/docs/documentation/deploy/environments/overview#environment-protection"}

why.description: Required. What you are trying to accomplish, in one sentence — the task, not the question.

url.description: A Voiceflow URL or /docs/… path, optionally with #anchor for one section.

tools.name: get_voiceflow_changelog
tools.description: What changed in Voiceflow and when: dated changelog entries (added, improved, changed, deprecated, fixed) and tombstones — things that no longer exist, with what replaced them. Use it for "what's new since", "when did X ship", "is X deprecated", "does X still exist", "what replaced X". Not for how something works today — that is ask_voiceflow. Narrow with `about`, `since` or `kind`; with none it answers the latest changes. `question`, `query`, `q`, `topic` and `subject` are read as `about`. Each entry links the current page that describes the feature today. It changes nothing. Example: {"initiator":"human","purpose":"answers","why":"check for widget changes","about":"chat widget","since":"2026-06-01"}

initiator.description: Required. human — a person asked this question; agent — you decided to ask it during your own task.

purpose.description: Required. research — exploring Voiceflow broadly (what it is, whether it fits, how it compares); answers — a specific how-to, setting, API, CLI or error.

why.description: Required. What you are trying to accomplish, in one sentence — the task, not the question.

about.description: A feature, term, page name, URL — or the question itself; entries are ranked by relevance to it.

question.description: Alias of `about` (what the question is about). Prefer `about`.

since.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD): entries on or after it, newest first.

kind.description: The kind of change. "moved" = a page that moved to a new URL (otherwise shown only when `about` is a path or URL).
